Domain-1.overview:
This domain evaluates the integration of security principles into the earliest stages of the product and software development lifecycle, ensuring security is never an afterthought.
  • Shift-Left Strategy: Embeds threat assessment and security criteria into initial design phases.
  • Developer Empowerment: Provides technical teams with integrated, automated tools to write secure code.
  • Flaw Eradication: Focuses on removing entire classes of vulnerabilities during compilation and build stages.
  • Accountability Framework: Establishes clear ownership for code quality and security risks.
Domain-1.title: Development Security
Domain-1.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are business and security requirements defined together before writing code?
  • Do product owners treat security features as first-class backlog priorities?
  • How do you track software security objectives from conception to release?
Domain-1.1-recommendation:
What is Secure-by-Design Product Requirements?

Secure-by-Design Product Requirements ensure that non-functional security goals are identified, documented, and prioritized alongside functional business features before a single line of code is written, eliminating costly architectural retrofitting later.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate that every new digital product or system business case includes a formalized, non-negotiable **Security Requirement Baseline** approved by the security team. Product managers must be held accountable for maintaining these objectives as part of core delivery metrics.

Technical Recommendations

Establish a standard library of reusable security user stories within product backlog management tools (e.g., Jira). Require that these foundational security criteria be linked explicitly to acceptance criteria for all major software epics.
Domain-1.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Is secure coding training tailored to the specific languages used by developers?
  • Do software engineers complete refresher courses on modern exploitation methods?
  • How do you measure developer competency in securing code pathways?
Domain-1.2-recommendation:
What is Integrated Developer Security Training?

Integrated Developer Security Training provides software engineers with role-specific, practical knowledge to write secure software code, identify common design flaws, and address software vulnerabilities directly within their development tools and workflows.

Executive Recommendations

Establish a rolling, mandatory training budget specifically for software developers that focuses on engineering-centric security rather than passive compliance checks. Link training completion explicitly to development team performance benchmarks.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy interactive, language-specific training applications directly accessible from the development environment. Sponsor an internal **Security Champions Program** where designated developers receive advanced training to advocate for best practices within their daily teams.
Domain-1.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Is source code scanned automatically for vulnerabilities on every commit?
  • Are build pipelines configured to fail if critical code flaws are introduced?
  • How do you prevent cryptographic keys or tokens from being committed to repositories?
Domain-1.3-recommendation:
What is Static Application Security Testing (SAST)?

Static Application Security Testing (SAST) involves automated code analysis tools that scan custom software source code to detect known patterns of security bugs, performance inefficiencies, and structural risks early in the development loop.

Executive Recommendations

Authorize policy mandates requiring automated SAST integration into all code repositories across the enterprise. Enforce a hard baseline policy stating that code with unmitigated high-severity findings cannot be released into production environments.

Technical Recommendations

Embed automated SAST scanners into continuous integration (CI) environments to validate pull requests automatically. Implement pre-commit hooks to scan local developer workstations for embedded hardcoded secrets or API tokens before they exit the local box.
Domain-1.3-vendor-solution: Red Hat Trusted Software Supply Chain
Domain-1.3-vendor-description: Provides integrated automated code analysis, scanning, and policy enforcement within development loops to catch flaws before code leaves development stages.
Domain-1.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are staging or pre-production applications scanned during runtime for flaws?
  • Do you perform automated fuzzing tests to stress application inputs?
  • How are runtime testing findings routed back to development teams?
Domain-1.4-recommendation:
What is Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST)?

Dynamic Application Security Testing (DAST) assesses an application from the outside while it is actively running, simulating real-world malicious inputs to find configuration defects, routing errors, and deployment vulnerabilities.

Executive Recommendations

Ensure that budget allocations support continuous automated black-box testing of all externally visible digital services. Require product teams to incorporate DAST remediation schedules into standard iteration and release velocity plans.

Technical Recommendations

Configure automated DAST tooling to spin up inside non-production environments immediately following successful deployments. Feed DAST API and runtime logs directly into developer tracking dashboards to speed up remediation validation loops.
Domain-1.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you map out application data flows and potential attack vectors before building?
  • Is a formal threat model updated whenever an architecture changes?
  • Who acts as the final sign-off authority for accepted threat risks?
Domain-1.5-recommendation:
What is Threat Modeling Integration?

Threat Modeling Integration is a structured engineering process where systems are systematically analyzed to identify hypothetical security threats, define defensive mitigation strategies, and document risk realities early in the cycle.

Executive Recommendations

Establish a corporate governance rule making architectural threat models mandatory for all applications handling sensitive customer data or critical infrastructure assets. Review summary threat registries at executive risk committee boards quarterly.

Technical Recommendations

Adopt structured threat modeling methodologies (such as STRIDE) and treat the models as documentation artifacts within software repositories. Conduct iterative, mini-threat reviews during system architecture modifications or major API changes.
Domain-1.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Does your enterprise policy mandate memory-safe programming languages where applicable?
  • Are modern compiler protections (e.g., ASLR, DEP) strictly enforced for binaries?
  • How do you audit custom enterprise software for unsafe function calling?
Domain-1.6-recommendation:
What is Safe Language Selection & Compiler Flags?

Safe Language Selection mandates using modern, memory-safe languages (e.g., Go, Rust, Java) to eradicate entire categories of memory bugs, combined with security hardening compiler configurations for low-level systems code.

Executive Recommendations

Publish a strategic engineering directive favoring memory-safe systems engineering for all net-new custom software projects. Establish explicit technological approval loops for any projects requiring unmanaged, legacy memory allocation patterns.

Technical Recommendations

Configure standard enterprise build configuration profiles that strictly enforce advanced compiler flags, such as stack canaries, position-independent executable execution, and memory safety tracking options at build time.
Domain-1.6-vendor-description: Includes a collection of pre-hardened base build environments and tools natively configured to build application binaries using modern, strict cryptographic and memory-protection flags.
Domain-1.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are development managers measured on security defect density rather than feature speed alone?
  • Do engineering dashboards track the mean-time-to-remediate (MTTR) software flaws?
  • Is software security posture directly linked to product launch readiness certificates?
Domain-1.7-recommendation:
What is Secure-by-Design Key Performance Indicators?

Secure-by-Design Key Performance Indicators are quantitative delivery performance metrics that bind software security performance directly to engineering velocity measurements, ensuring structural security matches commercial goals.

Executive Recommendations

Embed software security performance outcomes directly into executive and management compensation structures for digital engineering arms. Ensure application risk profiles must meet clear thresholds before products are approved for launch.

Technical Recommendations

Build real-time visibility dashboards tracking code security flaws over time, code coverage metrics for security assertions, and average flaw age. Automate the aggregation of pipeline status blocks to deliver real-time data to leaders.
Domain-1.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are applications subjected to manual penetration testing before every major version release?
  • Do you utilize specialized external application testers who specialize in logical flaws?
  • How do you verify the technical remediation of logic bypasses?
Domain-1.8-recommendation:
What is Independent Application Pen-Testing Audits?

Independent Application Pen-Testing Audits involve highly targeted, deep engineering assessments executed by objective human offensive security experts to discover contextual business-logic flaws that automated tooling cannot see.

Executive Recommendations

Provide dedicated board funding for rigorous manual application-level penetration assessments on high-priority platforms. Ensure validation exercises are decoupled from the core development organization to keep reporting objective.

Technical Recommendations

Require software engineering teams to provide deep API specifications, architectural schemas, and unprivileged access credentials to testing partners to enable maximum code paths coverage during targeted assessments.

Domain-2.overview:
This domain measures the organization's ability to ensure that infrastructure and platforms are inherently hardened right out of the box, requiring zero manual configuration change to achieve safety.
  • Zero-Config Security: Mandates that all systems deploy natively in their safest configuration stance.
  • Attack Vector Removal: Automatically disables legacy protocols, unnecessary utilities, and default access.
  • Immutability Enforcement: Replaces runtime configuration tinkering with immutable system baselines.
  • Drift Invalidation: Eradicates changes to operating systems via automated environment teardowns.
Domain-2.title: Configuration Security
Domain-2.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you deploy systems using standardized, pre-hardened operating images?
  • Are unnecessary packages, compilers, and shells stripped out of production systems?
  • How often are baseline security golden images updated and recertified?
Domain-2.1-recommendation:
What is Baseline Hardened Operating System Templates?

Baseline Hardened Operating System Templates are pre-configured virtual machine or container images constructed to adhere to international hardening checklists (e.g., CIS Benchmarks), ensuring baseline technical safety.

Executive Recommendations

Establish a policy that prohibits manual creation or deployment of unvetted raw operating systems in any production workspace. Mandate that all infrastructure uses centralized, digitally signed golden images.

Technical Recommendations

Utilize automated image builders to systematically generate minimal operating profiles. Ensure that server images exclude unnecessary networking protocols, debugging capabilities, or terminal applications.
Domain-2.1-vendor-description: Enables creation of custom, minimized, pre-hardened operating system images tailored for specific hybrid cloud locations to ensure consistency and safety.
Domain-2.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are legacy unencrypted transport protocols (e.g., HTTP, Telnet, FTP) blocked at system creation?
  • Is TLS 1.3 enforced by default for all communication paths?
  • How do you identify old or deprecated network services active within systems?
Domain-2.2-recommendation:
What is Default-Off Legacy Network Protocols?

Default-Off Legacy Network Protocols represents an architectural stance where insecure, ancient network routing patterns and unencrypted transmission capabilities are completely disabled out-of-the-box on all environments.

Executive Recommendations

Approve architectural standard directives that outlaw the use of unencrypted data transmission services inside organizational parameters. Require explicit cryptographic exceptions for any connectivity with legacy external environments.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy platform-level control configurations that natively block weak cryptographic suites and deprecated transport layer versions. Enforce automated enforcement engines that close non-standard or dangerous operational network ports.
Domain-2.3: Removal of Default Credentials and Test Accounts
Domain-2.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • How do you enforce the complete rotation of factory-default vendor accounts?
  • Are demo databases and sample application files automatically stripped from frameworks?
  • Does configuration testing look for trivial default credential sets across platforms?
Domain-2.3-recommendation:
What is Removal of Default Credentials?

Removal of Default Credentials is the automated process of validating that factory passwords, embedded system diagnostic accounts, and boilerplate test configurations are systematically destroyed or overwritten before software initialization.

Executive Recommendations

Incorporate strict verification clauses within technology delivery and vendor validation checklists demanding absolute confirmation that zero default system configurations or factory testing credentials survive into operational systems.

Technical Recommendations

Utilize validation tools that systematically attempt connections against newly provisioned targets using extensive lists of well-known manufacturer defaults. Design custom setup loops to force unique passphrase creation upon initial service start.
Domain-2.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are containers allowed to run with root-privileged access contexts?
  • Do you configure container runtimes with read-only file architectures?
  • Are applications packaged into 'distroless' images lacking system package managers?
Domain-2.4-recommendation:
What is Immutable Container Stance & Distroless Images?

Immutable Container Stance restricts workloads from changing their filesystem states during processing, combined with 'distroless' packaging models that eliminate host files and package tools entirely from container images.

Executive Recommendations

Direct system development guidelines to implement modern containerized infrastructure standards that mandate non-root execution frameworks across container platforms, reducing localized server hijacking capabilities.

Technical Recommendations

Configure pod deployment files to set read-only file parameters explicitly. Build container runtime boundaries using stripped base environments consisting solely of compiled binary logic and required execution references.
Domain-2.4-vendor-solution: Red Hat OpenShift & Universal Base Images (UBI)
Domain-2.4-vendor-description: Delivers minimalist, container-optimized system layers designed to enforce non-root security boundaries and enterprise stability out of the gate.
Domain-2.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Is infrastructure audited continuously against baseline targets like CIS or OpenSCAP?
  • How do you track discrepancies between expected and real-world configurations?
  • Are deviation alerts generated automatically for infrastructure engineering attention?
Domain-2.5-recommendation:
What is Automated Configuration Audit and Enforcement?

Automated Configuration Audit and Enforcement utilizes specialized programmatic verification blocks to continually evaluate target system parameters against defined technical baselines, warning operators of non-compliance.

Executive Recommendations

Require regular configuration safety compliance matrices to be delivered to leadership platforms. Ensure compliance assessments are driven by continuous automated validation engines rather than static manually managed reviews.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy continuous scanning modules across all running host systems using OpenSCAP frameworks. Centralize monitoring alerts to dynamically catch any user or utility that modifies local protection properties manually.
Domain-2.5-vendor-description: Provides automated evaluation of hybrid cloud system deployments against standard regulatory and custom configuration profiles.
Domain-2.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Does your infrastructure automatically overwrite unauthorized configuration changes automatically?
  • Are drift parameters corrected programmatically without waiting for human tickets?
  • How do you track automated adjustments triggered by environment self-healing events?
Domain-2.6-recommendation:
What is Dynamic Configuration Remediation Engine?

Dynamic Configuration Remediation Engine goes beyond simple monitoring to proactively revert configuration drift, using automation to overwrite unauthorized infrastructure modifications in real time.

Executive Recommendations

Authorize the implementation of self-healing automation patterns within infrastructure environments, providing technical teams the clearance to prioritize programmatic control enforcement over manual fixes.

Technical Recommendations

Incorporate continuous reconciliation controllers (such as GitOps operators) to oversee system properties. Configure these controllers to immediately restore baseline desired state whenever an unauthorized state change is discovered.
Domain-2.6-vendor-solution: Red Hat OpenShift GitOps & Ansible Automation Platform
Domain-2.6-vendor-description: Combines continuous desired-state tracking with automated loops to correct drift back to verified templates automatically.
Domain-2.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are bare-metal systems configured with unique, cryptographically managed BIOS keys?
  • Do you enforce hardware-root virtual machine protections at the host layer?
  • How do you track firmware version patch matrices on processing nodes?
Domain-2.7-recommendation:
What is Firmware & Hypervisor Hardening Protocols?

Firmware & Hypervisor Hardening Protocols ensures that protection structures protect layers beneath the operating system, focusing on securing system hypervisors, hardware microcode, and the initialization layers.

Executive Recommendations

Include physical firmware governance requirements into core compute hardware purchasing arrangements. Require suppliers to explicitly document their physical protection methodologies and secure update approaches.

Technical Recommendations

Enforce strict UEFI Secure Boot patterns across compute configurations. Enable low-level virtualization protection settings on core nodes to isolate hypervisor memory areas from potential guest system exploitation attempts.
Domain-2.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do production system nodes cycle out and recreate themselves on a scheduled timer?
  • What is the maximum lifespan of a running compute instance in your environment?
  • How do you guarantee that residual localized cached data vanishes entirely during node churn?
Domain-2.8-recommendation:
What is Self-Destructing & Zero-State Compute Execution?

Self-Destructing & Zero-State Compute Execution minimizes attacker persistence by systematically tearing down and rebuilding system components on a regular schedule, using ephemeral filesystems that wipe memory traces entirely upon deletion.

Executive Recommendations

Sponsor the strategic engineering shift toward fully ephemeral compute models, transforming organizational resilience from a state of preservation into a continuous state of programmatic replacement.

Technical Recommendations

Configure autoscaling clusters to systematically destroy and rebuild individual node members on a strict 24-to-48-hour schedule. Enforce strict stateless code designs that require all operational states to exist only in dedicated backend storage systems.

Domain-3.overview:
This domain validates system architecture models to ensure they enforce structural barriers, isolate workloads, and minimize the digital attack footprint by default.
  • Footprint Curtailment: Deliberately reduces active visibility vectors, ports, and discovery targets.
  • Micro-Segmentation: Enforces zero-trust isolation boundaries across container and cloud network flows.
  • Default Deny: Restricts internal component access explicitly to known, pre-approved data pathways.
  • Edge Separation: Decouples data processing engines completely from ingress edge layers.
Domain-3.title: Attack Surface Control
Domain-3.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are systems isolated from other workloads by default unless explicitly permitted?
  • Do you utilize software-defined filtering matrices to isolate application environments?
  • How are intra-host communication footprints visualized and limited?
Domain-3.1-recommendation:
What is Network Zero-Trust Micro-Segmentation?

Network Zero-Trust Micro-Segmentation breaks down digital networks into granular, isolated zones, controlling lateral communication paths via software policies regardless of physical server location.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate that all future multi-tier application architectures must deploy within micro-segmented infrastructure layers. Eliminate outdated 'flat' internal network topographies across corporate computing zones.

Technical Recommendations

Implement explicit container or network layer policies that block inter-namespace traffic by default. Require service applications to verify authorization paths for every inbound processing request.
Domain-3.1-vendor-description: Enforces software-defined network boundary separation natively at the pod level, applying strict default-deny connection rules between namespaces.
Domain-3.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are internal business logic microservices completely hidden behind a single entry point?
  • Do you strip system engineering metadata headers from edge outbound responses?
  • Are API access paths limited to explicitly declared functional patterns?
Domain-3.2-recommendation:
What is API Boundary Minimization?

API Boundary Minimization channels external system interactions through central, managed access proxies, ensuring raw application backends are never directly exposed to the internet.

Executive Recommendations

Incorporate centralized gateway verification policies into software deployment blueprints, ensuring all business unit API points run through centralized monitoring proxies.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy enterprise API gateway architectures that filter and sanitize incoming payloads. Configure boundary rules to intercept system error stack traces, replacing them with generic error indicators before they exit the environment.
Domain-3.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are incoming external connection routes limited solely to standard ports like 443?
  • Do edge filtering systems actively block connection requests originating from unmapped domains?
  • How are incoming traffic shapes evaluated for anomalies before reaching host networks?
Domain-3.3-recommendation:
What is Least Privilege Ingress Filtering?

Least Privilege Ingress Filtering ensures that internet entry configurations are limited strictly to the minimum essential transmission interfaces needed to service verified application workflows.

Executive Recommendations

Enforce mandatory network infrastructure evaluations to identify and shut down non-essential public-facing connection endpoints and exposed administrative systems.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy cloud firewalls and load balancing definitions configured with an explicit default-deny stance. Restrict administrative management access paths behind authenticated virtual private tunnels or verified zero-trust network brokers.
Domain-3.4: Service Mesh Isolation and Encrypted Transit
Domain-3.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Is internal application traffic encrypted in transit using mutual TLS (mTLS) automatically?
  • Do systems validate cryptographically signed identities for internal application-to-application calls?
  • Can you monitor and visualize all service-to-service communication paths in real time?
Domain-3.4-recommendation:
What is Service Mesh Isolation?

Service Mesh Isolation offloads cryptographic traffic management and authentication to an infrastructure sidecar proxy, enforcing mutual TLS (mTLS) across all internal microservice communication pathways automatically.

Executive Recommendations

Adopt platform architecture standards that mandate zero-trust internal encryption, ensuring data is protected in transit even inside the internal network perimeter.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy an enterprise service mesh layer across computing environments. Enforce strict mTLS rules that reject unencrypted or unauthenticated connections between internal components.
Domain-3.4-vendor-description: Provides native infrastructure proxy management to enforce mutual TLS, continuous path observation, and fine-grained communication rules by default.
Domain-3.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are data storage components isolated into distinct, un-routable network layers?
  • How do you prevent data leaks or cross-talk between different customer records?
  • Are shared system cache layers cleared between separate user processing cycles?
Domain-3.5-recommendation:
What is Data Tier Separation?

Data Tier Separation ensures database and storage systems operate within isolated network rings, completely hidden from frontend presentation environments and web applications.

Executive Recommendations

Establish strict data architecture rules that forbid placing databases or permanent file repositories in public-facing network segments.

Technical Recommendations

Isolate database networks behind multiple layers of security proxies. Implement database abstraction filters to prevent frontend components from querying backend data engines directly.
Domain-3.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you run continuous automated discovery to map your public attack surface?
  • Are newly provisioned cloud interfaces automatically flagged for security team evaluation?
  • How do you identify shadow IT or unvetted environments across cloud providers?
Domain-3.6-recommendation:
What is Attack Surface Mapping Automation?

Attack Surface Mapping Automation uses automated asset discovery to continuously scan public networks for unexpected endpoints, rogue cloud configurations, or unmanaged infrastructure assets.

Executive Recommendations

Fund continuous external exposure monitoring programs to maintain a real-time, accurate inventory of all public-facing corporate assets and domains.

Technical Recommendations

Integrate external attack surface discovery tools into security monitoring workflows. Configure automated alerts to trigger whenever an unauthorized sub-domain or cloud endpoint is discovered.
Domain-3.6-vendor-solution: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
Domain-3.6-vendor-description: Continuously visualizes container network topology and infrastructure deployments to pinpoint and minimize operational exposure risks.
Domain-3.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do highly sensitive workloads run inside hardware-isolated secure memory spaces?
  • Is data encrypted in memory during active runtime execution loops?
  • Can your underlying host platform or hypervisor administrators view active transactional data?
Domain-3.7-recommendation:
What is Hardware-Enforced Enclave Segmentation?

Hardware-Enforced Enclave Segmentation uses CPU-level security features to isolate processing threads inside encrypted memory spaces, keeping data hidden from hypervisors and host root users.

Executive Recommendations

Require hardware-isolated confidential computing runtimes for high-risk data processing workflows, such as financial transaction processing or core intellectual property operations.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy application workloads onto infrastructure configured with hardware isolation extensions (e.g., AMD SEV-SNP, Intel TDX) to encrypt data in use across the memory architecture.
Domain-3.7-vendor-description: Supports CPU-driven confidential execution technologies to shield sensitive runtime data from hypervisor or host-level access.
Domain-3.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are unused operating system kernel modules completely blocked from loading at runtime?
  • Do you enforce application sandbox execution frameworks like Seccomp or SELinux?
  • How do you verify that non-essential hardware calls are turned off across system nodes?
Domain-3.8-recommendation:
What is Unused Feature Deprecation?

Unused Feature Deprecation disables unused capabilities at the operating system kernel level, using runtime policy enforcement modules to block unexpected system calls and prevent exploit chains.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate that all production systems use advanced mandatory access control frameworks, and require explicit executive waivers to run systems with relaxed security profiles.

Technical Recommendations

Enforce strict SELinux policies across systems. Use system constraints to disable unused kernel capabilities, blocking custom firmware adjustments or unexpected kernel runtime alterations.
Domain-3.8-vendor-description: Enforces mandatory access control models natively, isolating process spaces and restricting access vectors regardless of user-level privileges.

Domain-4.overview:
This domain evaluates the verification and integrity of third-party software artifacts, libraries, and external developer dependencies, ensuring that zero unvetted code enters production workflows.
  • SBOM Generation: Produces a comprehensive Software Bill of Materials for every software release.
  • Provenance Verification: Validates cryptographic signatures to confirm code origin and authenticity.
  • Upstream Vetting: Replaces direct download paths with curated, scanned internal library repositories.
  • Vulnerability Tracing: Tracks software dependency trees to locate newly disclosed vulnerabilities across ecosystems.
Domain-4.title: Supply Chain Security
Domain-4.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you generate a machine-readable SBOM for every custom application build?
  • Are SBOM artifacts stored in an immutable registry alongside container images?
  • How do you audit external software packages for hidden open-source dependencies?
Domain-4.1-recommendation:
What is a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM)?

A Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) is an automated, machine-readable inventory list detailing every open-source package, third-party library, and internal code module nested inside a software application asset.

Executive Recommendations

Establish procurement regulations requiring all external software suppliers to provide certified, standard format SBOM data. Integrate SBOM tracking into core corporate risk registers.

Technical Recommendations

Incorporate SBOM generation tools (e.g., CycloneDX formats) into the build pipeline, ensuring an inventory catalog is automatically generated and archived on every application compilation pass.
Domain-4.1-vendor-solution: Red Hat Trusted Software Supply Chain
Domain-4.1-vendor-description: Automates SBOM tracking, verification, and artifact collection during build workflows to maintain accurate inventory records.
Domain-4.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are open-source libraries scanned continuously for known CVE defects before build staging?
  • Do build pipelines block compilation when dependencies contain critical security flaws?
  • How do you discover licensing risks inside third-party application modules?
Domain-4.2-recommendation:
What is Software Composition Analysis (SCA)?

Software Composition Analysis (SCA) automatically inventories the open-source software libraries within an application codebase, matching them against known vulnerability databases to flag bugs and licensing issues.

Executive Recommendations

Adopt zero-tolerance governance baselines regarding unpatched high-severity open-source components in production. Require product engineering groups to prioritize dependency remediation lifecycles.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy continuous SCA scanners within code repositories. Define build rule criteria to automatically halt build pipelines if dependency packages contain critical vulnerabilities without a valid exception flag.
Domain-4.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are developers blocked from downloading unvetted library packages directly from public internet sites?
  • Do you route dependency resolution paths through a centralized, scanned proxy repository?
  • How are newly updated external modules validated before internal distribution?
Domain-4.3-recommendation:
What is Curated Internal Dependency Registries?

Curated Internal Dependency Registries act as a verified proxy firewall, forcing development tools to fetch dependencies from a managed internal store rather than pulling directly from public internet hubs.

Executive Recommendations

Authorize infrastructure funding to establish dedicated internal artifact repositories, mandating their use across all software teams to prevent unvetted external code from entering codebases.

Technical Recommendations

Configure developer runtime properties and local proxies to direct package manager calls exclusively to trusted internal storage arrays. Automate scanning on these arrays to block malicious code variants.
Domain-4.3-vendor-description: Functions as a trusted, secure hosting platform for curated application artifacts and base runtime components, featuring integrated vulnerability scanning.
Domain-4.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are application artifacts cryptographically signed by build servers upon pipeline completion?
  • Does production infrastructure reject containers that lack a verified corporate build signature?
  • How do you protect signing keys from unauthorized developer access?
Domain-4.4-recommendation:
What is Cryptographic Artifact and Code Signing?

Cryptographic Artifact and Code Signing uses digital signatures (e.g., Sigstore frameworks) to lock down built software, ensuring running workloads are genuine and unchanged from their build pipeline origins.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate code signature verification policies for all production compute nodes, ensuring the infrastructure will reject unsigned code artifacts to protect against tampering.

Technical Recommendations

Integrate open signing workflows (such as Cosign/Sigstore) directly into deployment steps. Configure admission controllers on compute clusters to reject any container missing a valid cryptographic signature.
Domain-4.4-vendor-description: Delivers secure cryptographic signature workflows using Sigstore technology, allowing teams to verify software authenticity at scale.
Domain-4.5: Vulnerability Lifespan and Patching SLA Enforcement
Domain-4.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you strictly enforce a time-bound SLA to remediate newly discovered third-party CVEs?
  • Are application development teams forced to redeploy software if patch deadlines are missed?
  • How do you monitor outstanding technical security debt across different product groups?
Domain-4.5-recommendation:
What is Vulnerability Lifespan SLA Enforcement?

Vulnerability Lifespan SLA Enforcement establishes strict corporate timelines for patching external dependencies, backed by automated mechanisms that flag overdue components for remediation.

Executive Recommendations

Approve clear patch timeline policies (e.g., critical flaws must be patched within 72 hours). Hold engineering leaders accountable for tracking outstanding vulnerability backlogs against these targets.

Technical Recommendations

Build automated dashboard rollups that flag software deployments violating current patch compliance dates. Connect alert systems directly to engineering work queues to streamline ticket tracking.
Domain-4.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you compile the exact same binary twice from source code to yield matching cryptographic hashes?
  • Do you verify that build configurations exclude unpredictable variable inputs like timestamps?
  • How do you detect if a build server injects unauthorized changes during compilation?
Domain-4.6-recommendation:
What is Reproducible Build Verification?

Reproducible Build Verification configures compilation pipelines so that compiling the exact same source code produces identical binary outputs down to the byte, proving the compilation pipeline has not been tampered with.

Executive Recommendations

Support engineering initiatives to build fully deterministic compilation pipelines for critical platforms, establishing strong protection against build-infrastructure hijacking attempts.

Technical Recommendations

Standardize build environments using specific containerized build images. Configure build settings to normalize environmental variables, path references, and build timestamps during compilation phases.
Domain-4.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are build servers completely blocked from reaching the internet during artifact compilation?
  • How do you feed verified dependency manifests into isolated build execution nodes?
  • Are build inputs pinned strictly to pre-fetched, hash-verified local file mirrors?
Domain-4.7-recommendation:
What is Hermetic Build Architectures?

Hermetic Build Architectures run compilation tasks in isolated environments with network access disabled, ensuring compilers consume only pre-verified, local software artifacts.

Executive Recommendations

Authorize building specialized, network-isolated build farms for core software applications, ensuring complete isolation from public network injection risks.

Technical Recommendations

Configure continuous integration execution agents to disconnect external internet interfaces before starting code compilation tasks, forcing systems to fetch dependencies from validated local file caches.
Domain-4.7-vendor-description: Assists security teams in verifying component data relationships and provenance paths within strict, structured dependency ecosystems.
Domain-4.8: Upstream Dependency Sponsoring & Upstream Security Auditing
Domain-4.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you audit the security practices of open-source projects critical to your business?
  • Does your enterprise fund or contribute security fixes back to vital open-source projects?
  • How do you track author risk or hostile maintainer changes in external open-source libraries?
Domain-4.8-recommendation:
What is Upstream Dependency Sponsoring?

Upstream Dependency Sponsoring goes beyond simple security scanning by actively contributing to and auditing the development health of core open-source projects that form the foundation of organizational software stacks.

Executive Recommendations

Establish corporate guidelines that allocate formal engineering resources to support and review the security health of foundational open-source code libraries used by corporate platforms.

Technical Recommendations

Assign senior developers to review upstream package change histories and project governance models for foundational dependencies, helping to catch code quality shifts before packages roll into internal infrastructure libraries.

Domain-5.overview:
This domain evaluates the strength and architecture of cryptography across the enterprise, ensuring that data protection mechanisms are resilient against modern cryptanalysis and completely under localized authority.
  • Cryptographic Agility: Enables rapid updates to algorithms and keys without requiring core code refactoring.
  • Post-Quantum Preparedness: Prepares systems to integrate quantum-resistant algorithms across data assets.
  • Sovereign Identity: Ensures root identity services are anchored locally and free from external dependencies.
  • No-Cleartext Hardening: Mandates that data is never exposed in plaintext across any processing tier by default.
Domain-5.title: Cryptography & Identity
Domain-5.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are cryptographic algorithms decoupled from application source code files?
  • Can your security teams update an enterprise hashing configuration without rewriting application logic?
  • How do you track deprecated cipher usage across distributed software systems?
Domain-5.1-recommendation:
What is Agile Algorithmic Architecture?

Agile Algorithmic Architecture abstracts security algorithms away from application code into managed configuration layers, allowing security teams to upgrade cipher configurations without code changes.

Executive Recommendations

Adopt core architectural guidelines that prohibit hardcoding specific encryption ciphers or hash keys directly inside custom enterprise software repositories.

Technical Recommendations

Utilize standard system cryptographic sub-systems and verified security libraries that read cipher policies from centralized, host-level operating configuration files.
Domain-5.1-vendor-description: Provides system-wide cryptographic policies to enforce specific algorithmic baselines (e.g., FIPS compliance) across all running applications with a single configuration switch.
Domain-5.2: Hardware Root of Trust and Local Identity Providers
Domain-5.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are identity root certificates anchored inside locally controlled Hardware Security Modules (HSMs)?
  • Is enterprise single sign-on (SSO) independent of third-party public cloud hyperscaler infrastructure?
  • How do you isolate identity directories from external administrative access?
Domain-5.2-recommendation:
What is Hardware Root of Trust Identity?

Hardware Root of Trust Identity anchors enterprise authentication architectures and root validation keys inside locally managed physical security hardware, avoiding dependence on external cloud platform roots.

Executive Recommendations

Authorize capital allocation to ensure root identity services are anchored on locally controlled security hardware modules, establishing independent control over organizational credentials.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy localized identity federation solutions backed by physical HSM validation structures, ensuring authentication challenges can be verified even if connections to public cloud providers are lost.
Domain-5.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Is encryption-at-rest enforced natively by storage platforms without requiring user input?
  • Are encryption keys managed separately from the vendor hosting your raw data blocks?
  • How do you audit system components to verify that unencrypted storage volumes cannot be attached?
Domain-5.3-recommendation:
What is Default Encrypted-at-Rest Storage?

Default Encrypted-at-Rest Storage mandates that all virtual storage volumes, block stores, and backup datasets are automatically encrypted upon provisioning using keys managed separately from the infrastructure host.

Executive Recommendations

Enforce data protection policies that require automated encryption for all data storage layers, backed by independent key management infrastructure.

Technical Recommendations

Configure global storage management profiles to automatically apply strong encryption algorithms (e.g., AES-256) to all newly created virtual disks or persistent volumes, blocking unencrypted attachment paths.
Domain-5.3-vendor-description: Includes integrated data-at-rest storage volume encryption options that seamlessly connect with external, sovereign cryptographic key management infrastructure.
Domain-5.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do systems avoid using static, long-lived API tokens or access passwords?
  • Are service access tokens configured to automatically expire within minutes?
  • How do you manage automated renewal paths for software infrastructure tokens?
Domain-5.4-recommendation:
What is Ephemeral Machine Credentials?

Ephemeral Machine Credentials replaces permanent system-to-system access passwords with short-lived tokens generated dynamically on demand, minimizing the impact of credential leakage.

Executive Recommendations

Incorporate strict access control mandates requiring the removal of long-lived static system passwords or hardcoded API tokens from all enterprise infrastructure deployments.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy specialized secrets managers configured to issue dynamic, short-lived tokens for database and service authentication, utilizing automated rotation to minimize exposure windows.
Domain-5.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Is Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) mandated for all session connections across infrastructure?
  • Does a compromise of a master server key expose historical network traffic captures?
  • How do you audit transport channels for weak cryptographic handshakes?
Domain-5.5-recommendation:
What is Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS)?

Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) ensures that every network communication session uses a unique, ephemeral session key, preventing attackers from using a compromised master server key to decrypt historical traffic captures.

Executive Recommendations

Direct technology teams to implement advanced transit security configurations that enforce perfect forward secrecy across all corporate connection paths.

Technical Recommendations

Configure boundary load balancers and web service proxies to accept only advanced TLS configurations (e.g., ECDHE cipher suites) that natively support forward secrecy algorithms.
Domain-5.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are encryption keys rotated automatically on a strict schedule without manual tickets?
  • Is key access logged to immutable tracking systems for audit analysis?
  • How quickly can you revoke compromised master keys across distributed multi-cloud locations?
Domain-5.6-recommendation:
What is Centralized Cryptographic Key Lifecycle Management?

Centralized Cryptographic Key Lifecycle Management unifies key generation, rotation, and revocation within a sovereign system layer, ensuring clear visibility and control over all encryption keys.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate that all business systems use a centralized, audited key management framework, separating data storage layers from cryptographic access management control planes.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy dedicated key management servers that support standard integration protocols (e.g., KMIP) to automate key rotation schedules and centralize cryptographic tracking.
Domain-5.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Have you mapped your high-value long-term data assets for quantum risk?
  • Are you running hybrid cryptographic schemes combining current and quantum-resistant ciphers?
  • Does your infrastructure support testing new NIST-approved post-quantum algorithms?
Domain-5.7-recommendation:
What is Post-Quantum Cryptographic Readiness?

Post-Quantum Cryptographic Readiness inventories long-term data assets and prepares transport layers to support quantum-resistant encryption algorithms (e.g., ML-KEM) to protect data from future decryption risks.

Executive Recommendations

Approve a long-term strategic plan for quantum-safe technology migration, prioritizing the protection of sensitive data assets that remain vulnerable to retroactive decryption tactics.

Technical Recommendations

Begin testing post-quantum cryptographic configurations within non-production environment connections, using hybrid implementation profiles to assess performance footprints.
Domain-5.7-vendor-solution: Red Hat Enterprise Linux (Upstream cryptoreadiness focus)
Domain-5.7-vendor-description: Tracks and incorporates experimental post-quantum cryptographic libraries to help organizations prototype quantum-safe architectures early.
Domain-5.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Is sensitive data encrypted directly inside the application before reaching transport layers?
  • Does the database engine only see opaque, pre-encrypted fields for sensitive columns?
  • How do you manage decryption capabilities exclusively at trusted user execution points?
Domain-5.8-recommendation:
What is Application-Layer Object Encryption?

Application-Layer Object Encryption encrypts highly sensitive fields directly within the application runtime before storage or transmission, ensuring the data remains unreadable to intermediate databases or infrastructure hosts.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate application-level encryption controls for highly sensitive data classification tiers, ensuring data stays protected even if lower-level system boundaries are compromised.

Technical Recommendations

Implement client-side data protection routines within frontend applications, passing only pre-encrypted values to backend storage layers to protect data from database-level exposure.

Domain-6.overview:
This domain measures the deployment of automated testing pipelines and validation engines designed to enforce continuous security control validation and block non-compliant code shifts instantly.
  • Compliance-as-Code: Transforms security compliance checks into automated, testable engineering scripts.
  • Pipeline Interdiction: Empowers build pipelines to stop deployments that fail security validations.
  • Continuous Scanning: Replaces point-in-time security reviews with real-time, automated configuration scans.
  • Cryptographic Attestation: Validates build integrity automatically before approving container runs.
Domain-6.title: Automated Assurance
Domain-6.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are IaC definitions scanned automatically for misconfigurations before deployment?
  • Do tools block pipeline progression if unapproved network exposure models are introduced?
  • How do you maintain a standardized set of infrastructure rules across teams?
Domain-6.1-recommendation:
What is IaC Automated Verification?

IaC Automated Verification uses automated code analysis tools to scan infrastructure configurations (e.g., Terraform scripts) before deployment, catching misconfigurations like exposed database ports before infrastructure is provisioned.

Executive Recommendations

Enforce policy directives requiring all infrastructure configuration changes to pass through automated validation engines before deployment to production environments.

Technical Recommendations

Incorporate infrastructure scanning utilities into continuous delivery pipelines, checking infrastructure files against organization security policies before deployment execution.
Domain-6.1-vendor-description: Provides validation capabilities to pre-flight configuration manifests against technical policy targets prior to system adjustment execution.
Domain-6.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you run continuous automated scanning across cloud environments to catch open asset structures?
  • Are configuration anomalies flagged immediately to operational remediation teams?
  • How do you limit access privileges to prevent manual modifications to running infrastructure resources?
Domain-6.2-recommendation:
What is Automated Posture Scanning?

Automated Posture Scanning uses continuous monitoring agents to track resource configurations across cloud platforms, detecting misconfigurations and unauthorized public access points in real time.

Executive Recommendations

Require dashboard visibility for all cloud environments to ensure continuous tracking of compliance posture across the enterprise.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy cloud security posture management tools to monitor platform configurations, alerting teams to risks like unencrypted storage blocks or open security groups.
Domain-6.2-vendor-solution: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
Domain-6.2-vendor-description: Delivers continuous posture tracking across cloud environments, reporting configuration compliance issues and risk metrics automatically.
Domain-6.3: Hard Block Build Pipeline Failure Mechanisms
Domain-6.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do build pipelines halt automatically when critical vulnerabilities are discovered?
  • Can developers bypass security checks without formal management authorization records?
  • How do you audit build exception approvals across product groups?
Domain-6.3-recommendation:
What is Hard Block Build Failure?

Hard Block Build Failure configures continuous integration tools to fail builds automatically when code updates violate established security thresholds, preventing non-compliant updates from reaching production.

Executive Recommendations

Establish strict policy baselines that mandate automated deployment blocks for high-severity security findings, requiring formal approval for exceptions.

Technical Recommendations

Configure pipeline automation policies to return non-zero exit codes if security scans discover flaws above specified thresholds, halting the deployment pipeline automatically.
Domain-6.3-vendor-description: Enables integration of strict automated gate parameters within Tekton-driven workflows to stop non-compliant application deployments.
Domain-6.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are regulatory compliance audits performed using executable code scripts?
  • Can you generate automated compliance reports for audit teams on demand?
  • How are changes to compliance definition scripts managed and reviewed?
Domain-6.4-recommendation:
What is Compliance-as-Code Frameworks?

Compliance-as-Code Frameworks converts regulatory requirements into executable test scripts, replacing manual compliance check spreadsheets with automated, continuous auditing verification loops.

Executive Recommendations

Approve a strategic shift toward automated compliance models, replacing manual audit workflows with continuous, code-driven validation systems.

Technical Recommendations

Maintain system test compliance specifications using OpenSCAP formats within version control profiles, automating validation runs against target systems nightly.
Domain-6.4-vendor-description: Includes integrated OpenSCAP tools to automate security baseline compliance scanning against major regulatory standards natively.
Domain-6.5: Continuous Deployment Validation via Admission Control
Domain-6.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Does your infrastructure validate runtime security profiles before launching container images?
  • Are non-compliant container configurations blocked from starting at the platform level?
  • How do you handle real-time configuration overrides within cluster environments?
Domain-6.5-recommendation:
What is Admission Control Deployment Validation?

Admission Control Deployment Validation implements runtime infrastructure checks that intercept cluster deployment requests, evaluating application parameters against security rules before allowing the workloads to initialize.

Executive Recommendations

Mandate the use of policy-driven admission controllers across all production container environments to block unvalidated deployment configurations.

Technical Recommendations

Configure admission control webhooks to reject container deployment actions if configuration files require unsafe root privileges or use unvalidated network access models.
Domain-6.5-vendor-solution: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
Domain-6.5-vendor-description: Uses native admission control hooks to prevent non-compliant container deployments from running within managed compute nodes.
Domain-6.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do automated scripts continuously check for old or expired system passwords?
  • Are expired system credentials revoked automatically without requiring human action?
  • How do you log password rotation actions across separate applications?
Domain-6.6-recommendation:
What is Automated Secret Rotation Validation?

Automated Secret Rotation Validation utilizes background processing loops to continuously audit system credentials, verifying compliance with rotation schedules and programmatically revoking out-of-date tokens.

Executive Recommendations

Require automated password rotation mechanisms for all production databases and microservices, reducing the window of exposure for leaked credentials.

Technical Recommendations

Connect application secret storage vaults to background audit loops, automating key rotation tasks and alerting teams to legacy keys that require manual removal.
Domain-6.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do deployment servers verify the cryptographically signed history of build tasks?
  • Can infrastructure verify that an image passed vulnerability scanning before launch?
  • How do you protect build signature keys from injection modifications?
Domain-6.7-recommendation:
What is Cryptographic Pipeline Attestation?

Cryptographic Pipeline Attestation collects verifiable digital evidence at each stage of the build process (e.g., test passes, vulnerability checks), generating a signed package profile that infrastructure validates before running the code.

Executive Recommendations

Establish strict software supply chain policies that require valid cryptographic build attestations for all code running in critical production environments.

Technical Recommendations

Implement attestation frameworks (such as Tekton Chains) within build pipelines, configuring runtime admission platforms to reject applications that lack verified compliance records.
Domain-6.7-vendor-solution: Red Hat Trusted Software Supply Chain
Domain-6.7-vendor-description: Provides automated build attestation tracking using Tekton workflows, securing the path from development source code to production deployment.
Domain-6.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Does your infrastructure automatically reset modified system settings without waiting for admin intervention?
  • Are non-compliant network changes immediately isolated by automated scripts?
  • How do you audit remediation actions taken by self-healing automation engines?
Domain-6.8-recommendation:
What is Real-Time Remediation Guardrails?

Real-Time Remediation Guardrails uses active policy enforcement systems to block non-compliant configuration changes in real time, automatically resetting modified parameters to their approved states.

Executive Recommendations

Authorize the deployment of active, automated self-healing enforcement loops across enterprise platforms to minimize exposure windows and reduce configuration drift risks.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy policy tools configured to intercept and reject configuration drift, using automated workflows to restore baseline parameters immediately upon detecting unauthorized changes.
Domain-6.8-vendor-description: Uses continuous GitOps reconciliation loops to detect configuration drift and automatically reset running system states back to verified code patterns.

Domain-7.overview:
This domain assesses system resilience models, failure testing practices, and architecture designs that limit breach impact and ensure critical business systems remain available during security incidents.
  • Blast Radius Control: Limits security breaches to localized zones using structural boundaries.
  • Graceful Degradation: Configures applications to maintain core operations when supporting services fail.
  • Chaos Testing: Validates system resilience through simulated infrastructure failures and automated incident injection.
  • Sovereign Redundancy: Maintains independent failover computing capabilities completely under local control.
Domain-7.title: Resilience & Threat Modeling
Domain-7.1-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are workloads configured to prevent single-component failures from impacting adjacent services?
  • Do you enforce resource limits to block malicious resource exhaustion attacks?
  • How do you verify isolation boundaries between different processing nodes?
Domain-7.1-recommendation:
What is Container-Level Fault Isolation?

Container-Level Fault Isolation restricts compute and storage boundaries at the container runtime level, preventing compromised software tasks from exhausting host resources or impacting adjacent workloads.

Executive Recommendations

Require workload sizing limits and process isolation rules across all multi-tenant platforms to ensure system reliability and protection against resource starvation attacks.

Technical Recommendations

Configure explicit resource limit definitions (CPU and memory bounds) for all container deployments, utilizing runtime namespaces to keep process faults localized.
Domain-7.1-vendor-description: Enforces process isolation boundaries and resource constraints natively at the container level using Linux control group architecture.
Domain-7.2-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can applications maintain essential business operations if underlying database connectivity is lost?
  • Do frontend services display helpful, safe error pages without exposing configuration details during outages?
  • How do you validate application functionality under simulated dependency failure conditions?
Domain-7.2-recommendation:
What is Graceful Application Degradation?

Graceful Application Degradation designs software architectures to stay operational during partial infrastructure outages, using fallback modes to maintain core features when non-essential dependencies fail.

Executive Recommendations

Incorporate availability requirements into system designs, ensuring applications can deliver core services during backend component dependencies failure events.

Technical Recommendations

Implement circuit breaker development patterns and timeout constraints within code workflows, allowing services to drop non-essential integrations and fall back to safe default modes during performance drops.
Domain-7.3-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Are services distributed across separate geographical data centers to protect against outages?
  • Do data traffic routers fail over automatically if an entire infrastructure region goes offline?
  • How often do you test high-availability failover mechanisms under active operational loads?
Domain-7.3-recommendation:
What is Multi-Zone Infrastructure Redundancy?

Multi-Zone Infrastructure Redundancy distributes workload deployments across distinct geographical zones, using automated routing adjustments to maintain system uptime during localized physical outages.

Executive Recommendations

Authorize the deployment of high-availability configurations for all core business systems, ensuring operations can withstand localized computing platform outages.

Technical Recommendations

Deploy application clusters across multiple availability zones, utilizing intelligent request load balancing systems to redirect traffic during node cluster drops.
Domain-7.3-vendor-description: Supports multi-zone cluster deployment patterns to deliver platform resilience and automated load migration across physical data spaces.
Domain-7.4-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do communication proxies automatically stop routing requests to failing services?
  • Are failing microservices isolated from network queues to allow them to recover safely?
  • How do you monitor network call failure distributions across internal systems?
Domain-7.4-recommendation:
What is Network Circuit Breaker Policy?

Network Circuit Breaker Policy uses routing proxies to intercept communication failures, halting connection queues to failing services to prevent localized bugs from cascading across the enterprise platform.

Executive Recommendations

Incorporate circuit breaker integration requirements into core application transport baselines to protect system performance and stop cascading performance failures.

Technical Recommendations

Configure circuit breaker parameters within service mesh management filters, instructing proxies to drop connection queues to non-responsive services and return fast-fail notifications.
Domain-7.4-vendor-description: Includes built-in circuit breaker features to isolate failing service paths, helping engineers maintain system stability during component outages.
Domain-7.5-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can security detection systems automatically isolate a compromised host node?
  • Are data connection paths terminated programmatically when unusual data transfer rates are detected?
  • How do you validate automated isolation routines without breaking core customer interactions?
Domain-7.5-recommendation:
What is Automated Blast Radius Isolation?

Automated Blast Radius Isolation uses monitoring analytics to detect active system compromises, automatically modifying access rules and dropping connection paths to isolate infected nodes and protect the remaining network infrastructure.

Executive Recommendations

Approve automated containment protocols within incident response frameworks, authorizing technical systems to programmatically isolate high-risk infrastructure components during active cyber attacks.

Technical Recommendations

Connect runtime threat detection engines to network security configurations, orchestrating automated rules to block data transfer paths upon discovering container compromise events.
Domain-7.5-vendor-solution: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Security for Kubernetes
Domain-7.5-vendor-description: Monitors container runtimes for anomalous behavior, enabling automated containment actions to block compromised workloads in real time.
Domain-7.6-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you maintain an emergency processing platform completely independent of public cloud hyperscalers?
  • Can you restore business data maps onto local infrastructure during a major international vendor dispute?
  • How do you keep local backup systems synchronized without establishing continuous outbound connections?
Domain-7.6-recommendation:
What is Sovereign Air-Gapped Failover?

Sovereign Air-Gapped Failover maintains a disconnected emergency computing environment under complete local legal authority, providing a resilient processing platform during geopolitical disputes or major cloud platform outages.

Executive Recommendations

Fund an independent, locally controlled disaster backup facility to guarantee business continuity during major international vendor platform disruptions.

Technical Recommendations

Construct an isolated, locally hosted compute cluster capable of running core business apps. Populate data records via scheduled batch updates over secure, monitored transfer routes, keeping the platform isolated between sync cycles.
Domain-7.7-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Do you inject random system failures into production environments to test resilience?
  • Are application systems engineered to survive random container terminations without user impact?
  • How are findings from chaos engineering tests tracked and resolved?
Domain-7.7-recommendation:
What is Automated Chaos Engineering?

Automated Chaos Engineering injects deliberate infrastructure failures (e.g., stopping nodes, delaying network packets) into running environments to verify system self-healing capabilities and evaluate resilience assumptions.

Executive Recommendations

Support chaos engineering programs to validate system resilience under real-world pressure conditions, treating system fragility findings as high-priority engineering objectives.

Technical Recommendations

Integrate automated failure injection tools into staging and production clusters, assessing application recovery loops when individual processing components are terminated randomly.
Domain-7.8-summary:
Points to consider:
  • Can you rebuild your entire hybrid cloud environment from scratch using version-controlled code codebases?
  • Are configuration databases decoupled from computing infrastructure to allow rapid data migration?
  • What is your verified recovery time objective (RTO) for a complete system rebuild from source?
Domain-7.8-recommendation:
What is Immutable System State Reconstruction?

Immutable System State Reconstruction provides the tools and processes to rebuild the entire enterprise infrastructure stack from scratch using code templates stored in secure version-controlled repositories, ensuring clean recovery after major compromises.

Executive Recommendations

Require yearly 'clean-slate' restoration exercises to confirm the business can fully rebuild infrastructure dependencies from source files without using legacy server configurations.

Technical Recommendations

Maintain comprehensive declarative templates (e.g., Ansible Playbooks, GitOps manifests) for all infrastructure layers, automating setup routines to rebuild environments on clean infrastructure targets on demand.
Domain-7.8-vendor-solution: Red Hat Advanced Cluster Management for Kubernetes & Ansible Automation Platform
Domain-7.8-vendor-description: Combines declarative cluster automation tools with infrastructure-as-code pipelines to enable rapid deployment and orchestration across hybrid environments.
